title: Events & Execution Flow ⚡
description: Harness the power of BeginPlay, Tick, and custom events to drive your game.

slides.title: What Is an Event? 🎟️
slides.content:
# The Starting Gun

An **Event** node starts execution. Without an event, nothing happens. Think of events as **triggers**:

* **Event BeginPlay** – fires once when the game starts (or actor spawns)
* **Event Tick** – fires every frame (caution: heavy!)
* **Event ActorBeginOverlap** – fires when another actor overlaps
* **Custom Events** – you define when they fire

Each event has a white **output execution pin** (▶). Connect it to actions to build a chain.

quizData.question: When does Event BeginPlay fire?

options.text: Once when the game starts or the actor spawns
When you press Play in the editor

quizData.explanation: BeginPlay fires once when gameplay begins, after the actor is initialized.

slides.title: Your First Node Graph 🔗
slides.content:
## Hello, World!

Let's build the classic "Hello World" in Blueprints:

1. Open your `BP_FirstBlueprint`.
2. Right‑click → type **Event BeginPlay** → select it.
3. Drag off the white ▶ pin and release → type **Print String** → select.
4. In the Print String node, type `"Hello, Unreal!"` in the In String box.
5. **Compile** (toolbar button) to check for errors.
6. Drag the Blueprint into your level and press Play.

You should see "Hello, Unreal!" printed in the top‑left of the viewport! 🎉

slides.title: Node Setup
slides.content: The graph should look like this:
slides.codeSnippet:
Event BeginPlay → Print String
                   In String = "Hello, Unreal!"

quizData.question: To display a message on screen during gameplay, use the _____ _____ node.
quizData.explanation: Print String outputs text to the screen and log. It's the simplest way to debug.

slides.title: Event Tick – A Double‑Edged Sword ⏱️
slides.content:
## Every Frame, Every Time

**Event Tick** fires 30, 60, or even 120+ times per second, depending on frame rate.

* Use it for continuous movement, like rotating a fan.
* **Avoid heavy logic** in Tick – it can kill performance.
* Connect the **Delta Seconds** output pin (time since last frame) to ensure frame‑rate independent movement.

Example: `Set Actor Rotation` with `Delta Seconds * Rotation Speed`.

*Rule of thumb:* If it doesn’t need to happen every frame, use a **Timer** instead.

quizData.question: Event Tick runs only once per second.
quizData.explanation: Tick runs every frame, typically 30–120+ times per second, depending on performance.

slides.title: Custom Events 🛠️
slides.content:
## Call Your Own Shots

Right‑click → **Add Custom Event** → name it (e.g., `TurnOnLight`).

* You get a **red event node** that you can call from anywhere.
* Call it using the **Call Function** node (just type the event name).
* Perfect for organising logic and triggering sequences.

You can even add **input parameters** (variables passed to the event) in its Details panel.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Sequences to Chain

A **Sequence** node (right‑click → Sequence) splits one execution wire into multiple. Great for doing several things from one event. Each output fires in order.
